Community FHIR-to-OpenAPI generators exist but are not vendor-published (SKILL.md §2); followed back to HL7's own machine-readable definitions.

HL7's own complete R4 (v4.0.1) JSON Schema (draft-06): 680 definitions covering all 145 resource types, datatypes and backbone elements. Saved verbatim as upstream.json (sha256:2230406893b4cf002a4ee1e5e2bbeca22ac5d2d4931b3e9ef7b9594bbc376a01) and converted to components.schemas.

HL7's base CapabilityStatement for R4 ('a server that provides the full set of functionality defined by FHIR'): 145 resource types, their interactions, 1697 resource search parameters, the system interactions and the 46-entry operation list. Saved verbatim as upstream-capabilities.json (sha256:29ae88d66f66371f97a71feece55f2464ae35e8fadf40ddb79d4a005c1a5c217) and converted to the path surface.
All 46 R4 OperationDefinitions fetched individually (https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/operation-<resource>-<code>.json) for the $-operation paths, levels, input/output parameters and response resource.
The normative RESTful API specification: URL shapes per interaction, patch, the conditional create/update/delete forms, the _search POST form and the GET-invocation rule for operations.

notes: HL7 FHIR Release 4 (v4.0.1) RESTful API: the surface of the FHIR R4 server a fhir-fr workflow sends FR Core (hl7.fhir.fr.core 2.0.0) resources to. The fhir-fr adaptor is a builder library — it exports resource builders and common helpers but no HTTP operation (ast.json has none), so the external system is the R4 server named by its baseUrl/apiPath configuration, reached in practice with a FHIR client such as the fhir adaptor. FR Core publishes only profiles, extensions and terminology (no CapabilityStatement/SearchParameter/OperationDefinition), so the REST surface is the R4 base; this spec reuses HL7's R4 fhir.schema.json and base CapabilityStatement verbatim (the same bytes and hashes as specs/adaptors/fhir). 'Full' means all 145 R4 resource types with the eight base interactions plus patch and the conditional forms, the system interactions, /metadata and all 46 R4 operations: 1872 operations over 944 paths and all 680 upstream definitions. Conversion: the same derivation as specs/adaptors/fhir (a converter that regenerates that adaptor's committed openapi.json byte-for-byte from the same R4 inputs was used, so the two specs share every path, operationId, parameter and schema): draft-06 `const` became a single-value `enum`; `type: object` was added to object definitions; FHIR's 20 primitive types are inlined at their use sites; every body and response is offered as application/json and application/fhir+json; operations take a `Parameters` body, and a GET form is emitted only when every required input is primitive and the operation does not change state. One deliberate difference from specs/adaptors/fhir: the system-level operations (/$meta, /$versions, /$graphql, /$data-requirements, /$closure, /$process-message, /$convert) do not carry the `resourceType` path parameter, which the fhir spec declares on those paths although they have no `{resourceType}` segment. FR Core profile constraints (fr-core-patient, fr-core-organization, ...) are not encoded as schemas; payloads are described by the base R4 resource schemas. The adaptor pins FR Core 2.0.0 while 2.2.0 (trial-use) and 3.0.0-ballot exist; neither changes the REST surface.
